It progresses through three overlapping phases to maximize volume, progressively overload, and manage fatigue. Each week includes 4 training days (push, pull, legs, and an optional accessory/conditioning day). You can adjust days to fit the client’s schedule, but keep the weekly structure consistent.

Program overview
- Phases: 3 x 4 weeks (Phase 1: Foundation & hypertrophy mechanics; Phase 2: Increased volume and complexity; Phase 3: Peak hypertrophy with advanced techniques and higher RIR tolerance)
- Split: 4 days per week (Push, Pull, Legs, Accessory/Conditioning)
- Reps: 8–12 range for most sets, with occasional 6–8 and 12–15 back-off/repetition targets to vary stimulus
- Intensity: RIR-based progression (start around 1–2 RIR for main sets, aiming toward 0–1 RIR by the end of Phase 3)
- Progression: Weekly relative increases in volume or load, with planned deloads

- Estimated starting calories: +250–500 kcal above maintenance per day to support lean mass gains while minimizing fat gain. The exact surplus depends on body weight, body composition, and training load. A conservative starting point is:
  - Men: maintenance calories × 1.05–1.15
  - Women: maintenance calories × 1.05–1.15

- Fat gain control: aim for ~0.25–0.5 lb (0.1–0.2 kg) lean mass gain per week as a realistic target for an intermediate lifter. If too fat too fast, reduce calories by 100–200 kcal/day or increase training volume slightly.

2) Protein
- Daily intake: 1.6–2.2 g per kg body weight (0.73–1.0 g per lb).
- Distribution: aim for 3–5 protein-containing meals per day, with 0.25–0.6 g/kg per meal (roughly 25–40 g protein per meal, depending on body weight and size).
- Protein timing: consume a protein-rich meal or shake within 1–2 hours post-workout to optimize muscle protein synthesis; also include protein before sleep (25–40 g) when possible.

3) Carbohydrates
- Role: fuel workouts, replenish glycogen, support training volume, and aid recovery.
- Daily intake: 3–6 g/kg body weight, adjusted for training intensity and total calories.
  - Peak training days: toward the higher end (4–6 g/kg).

  - Post-workout: higher carb intake post-workout to replenish glycogen and support recovery (within 1–2 hours). Pair with protein.

4) Fats
- Daily intake: 0.8–1.0 g/kg body weight (or ~25–35% of total calories, depending on preferences and tolerance).
- Focus on healthy fats: fatty fish, nuts/seeds, olive oil, avocado, flax/chia seeds.

5) Fiber and micronutrients
- Target 25–40 g of fiber per day from vegetables, fruits, whole grains, legumes, and seeds.
- Ensure micronutrient sufficiency with a varied diet and consider a multivitamin if gaps exist.

6) Meal structure examples (one-day template)
- Meal 1 (breakfast): protein + complex carbs + fats
  - Example: 4 eggs or 1 cup egg whites + 2 whole eggs, oats with berries, 1 tbsp peanut/almond butter
- Meal 2 (mid-morning): protein + carbs
  - Example: Greek yogurt or whey shake, fruit, granola or muesli
- Meal 3 (pre-workout): protein + carbs, moderate fat
  - Example: chicken or tofu, rice or potatoes, vegetables, small olive oil portion
- Post-workout meal: protein + fast-acting carbs
  - Example: whey protein shake + banana or honey, rice, or white rice with chicken
- Meal 5 (dinner): protein + vegetables + fats
  - Example: salmon or lean beef, quinoa or sweet potato, steamed vegetables, olive oil

  - Example: casein protein shake or cottage cheese with nuts

- Intra-workout (optional for long sessions): small amounts of fast-digesting carbs if needed (e.g., a small Gatorade or dextrose/waxy maize snack) for sessions >90 minutes.
- Post-workout: 0.25–0.4 g/kg carbohydrate and 0.3–0.5 g/kg protein within 60 minutes; if not possible, aim for the next meal within 2 hours.

8) Hydration
- Baseline: 2–3 liters/day; adjust upward with training and heat.
- Include electrolytes if training is intense or lengthy.

- Omega-3s: 1–2 g/day (EPA+DHA) for inflammation and recovery.

- Weeks 1–4: establish intake targets, monitor body weight daily or 3–4 times weekly. If weight increases 0.25–0.5 lb per week and body composition looks favorable, maintain. If gaining too fast (>0.5 lb/week with visible fat gain), reduce surplus by 100–200 kcal/day.

- Weeks 9–12: fine-tune to maximize lean gains; consider a slight creeping surplus early in Week 9 if progress stalls, or implement a micro-deload in calories if fatigue is high, while keeping protein high.

Here is the full 12-week hypertrophy program, incorporating the travel block (weeks 5–6) with dumbbell-only hotel gym constraints, plus a structured return-deload and ramp back to the original trajectory. The plan preserves a hypertrophy focus (8–12 reps) with phase-by-phase progression, while ensuring practical feasibility given equipment limitations during weeks 5–6 and a careful re-entry in weeks 7–12.

Program structure at a glance
- Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 — Foundation and hypertrophy mechanics with a standard 4-day split (Push, Pull, Legs, Accessory/Mobility) plus optional conditioning days.
- Phase 2: Weeks 5–6 — Travel block (hotel gym, dumbbells only). 4 lifting days (Push, Pull, Legs, Optional Mobility/Full Body) + 2 conditioning days; emphasis on tempo, time-under-tension, unilateral work, and volume control. No barbell or machines.
- Phase 3: Weeks 7–12 — Return to full plan trajectory, with a deliberate ramp-back to the Phase 2/Phase 3 targets. Week 7 re-entry, Week 8 deload or light progression, Weeks 9–12 progressing back toward original targets, including possible introduction of advanced hypertrophy techniques and higher RIR tolerance management.

Key: training days per week
- Phase 1: 4 lifting days + 2 conditioning days (A and B) + optional accessory/conditioning on off days if desired.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–6): 4 lifting days (Push, Pull, Legs, Optional Full-Body/Accessory) + 2 conditioning days. Conditioning can be scheduled on separate days or after lifting depending on recovery.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–12): 4 lifting days (Push, Pull, Legs, Accessory) + 2 conditioning days. Optional mobility/active recovery day as needed.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 — Foundation, technique, hypertrophy base
Goal: Establish technique, base hypertrophy stimulus, joint tolerance for higher volume.

Week 1
- Push Day
  - Bench Press: 4 x 8–10 @ 70–75% 1RM (RIR 2)
  - Overhead Press: 3 x 8–10 @ 65–70% 1RM (RIR 2)
  - Dumbbell Incline Press: 3 x 10–12
  - Dumbbell Lateral Raises: 3 x 12–15
  - Triceps Pushdown or Dumbbell Skull Crushers: 3 x 12–15
- Pull Day
  - Deadlift (or Romanian Deadlift): 3 x 8–10 @ 70% 1RM (RIR 2)
  - Pull-ups/Chin-ups: 3 x 6–8
  - Barbell Row or Dumbbell Row: 3 x 8–10
  - Seated Cable Row or Dumbbell Row: 3 x 10–12
  - Face Pulls: 3 x 12–15
- Legs Day
  - Back Squat: 4 x 8–10 @ 70–75% 1RM (RIR 2)
  - Leg Press or Hack Squat: 3 x 10–12
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3 x 8–10
  - Leg Curls: 3 x 12–15
  - Calf Raises: 4 x 12–15
- Accessory/Conditioning
  - Conditioning A: 20–25 min steady-state or 10–12 min intervals (varied modalities)
  - Core: 3 x 12–15 (planks, Pallof press, cable anti-rotation)

Week 2
- Push Day
  - Bench Press: 4 x 8 @ 72–77% 1RM (RIR 2)
  - Overhead Press: 3 x 8–9 @ 68–72% 1RM (RIR 2)
  - Incline Dumbbell Press: 3 x 10–12
  - Dumbbell Flyes: 3 x 12–15
  - Lateral Raises: 3 x 12–15
  - Triceps Pushdown: 3 x 12–15
- Pull Day
  - Deadlift/RDL: 3 x 6–8 @ 70–75% 1RM (RIR 2)
  - Pull-ups/Chin-ups: 3 x 6–8
  - Barbell Row: 3 x 8–10
  - Seated Cable Row: 3 x 10–12
  - Face Pulls: 3 x 12–15
- Legs Day
  - Front Squat or Back Squat: 4 x 8–10
  - Leg Press: 3 x 10–12
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3 x 8–10
  - Leg Extensions: 3 x 12–15
  - Calf Raises: 4 x 12–15
- Accessory/Conditioning
  - Conditioning B: 15–20 min moderate cardio
  - Core: 3 x 12–15

Week 3
- Push Day
  - Bench Press: 4 x 8 @ 75–78% 1RM (RIR 2)
  - Overhead Press: 3 x 8 @ 70–75% 1RM (RIR 2)
  - Incline DB Press: 3 x 10–12
  - Dips or Floor Press: 3 x 10–12
  - Lateral Raises: 3 x 12–15
  - Triceps Extension: 3 x 12–15
- Pull Day
  - SLDL or Conventional Deadlift: 3 x 6–8 @ 65–75% 1RM (RIR 2)
  - Pull-ups/Chin-ups: 3 x 6–8
  - Row Variation (Barbell or DB): 3 x 8–10
  - Cable Row: 3 x 10–12
  - Face Pulls: 3 x 12–15
- Legs Day
  - Back Squat: 4 x 8–9
  - Leg Curl: 3 x 12–15
  - Leg Extensions: 3 x 12–15
  - Hip Thrust or Glute Bridge: 3 x 10–12
  - Calf Raises: 4 x 12–15
- Accessory/Conditioning
  - 10–15 min finisher (sled, battle ropes, or incline hill walk)
  - Core: 3 x 12–15

Week 4 — Deload
- Reduce main lift volume by 40–60%, keep intensity around 60–70% 1RM
- Optional light cardio and mobility work
- Maintain consistency; ensure recovery and sleep quality

Phase 2: Weeks 5–6 — Travel block (dumbbell/hotel gym)
Goal: Maintain hypertrophy stimulus, maximize time-under-tension with dumbbells, and manage fatigue while travel.

Week 5 — Travel Week 1

Notes for Weeks 5–6 travel
- Tempo: emphasize 2–0–2 tempo with 1-second pause, and extend eccentric to 3–4 seconds on key moves to maximize time under tension.
- RIR: Keep main lifts around RIR 1–2; stay conservative due to travel fatigue.
- Volume: If weight limits limit reps, add sets or extend reps within the 8–12 window.

Load progression and progression cues
- Progressive overload: aim for small weekly increases (2.5–5 lbs per dumbbell or 1–2 reps extra per set when using the 8–12 range).
- Tempo-based overload: use 2–0–2 tempo with 1-second pause, or 3–4 second eccentrics on some sets to drive stimulus when weights are limited.
- Re-test and reset: only re-test major 1RMs after a stable 2–4 weeks of consistent progression to avoid fatigue bias.

Nutrition and recovery (to accompany the 12 weeks)
- Calorie targets: slight surplus of 250–500 kcal/day above maintenance for lean mass gain; adjust as needed for fat gain control.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day; distribute across 3–5 meals; post-workout protein; consider a protein before bed.
- Carbs: 3–6 g/kg/day depending on training load; higher on heavier days; pre/post-workout timing.
- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day; include healthy fats.
- Hydration: 2–3 L/day baseline; more with higher training load.
- Sleep: 7–9 hours/night
- Supplements: protein powder, creatine (3–5 g/day), omega-3s, vitamin D as needed, multivitamin if needed.
